Part Three

Prevention of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

Paragraph 1

General

Article 34

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women is conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 33

1. The Regent conducts monitoring of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women in the Region.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted periodically on PD through the Office.
4. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of women for the current year.

Paragraph 3

Pokja PUG

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is North Central Timor Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of North Central Timor Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Central Timor. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of North Central Timor Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of North Central Timor Regency. 6. Office/Department is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and Child Protection. 7. Head of Office/Department is the Head of Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment. 8. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency. 9. Head of Regional Apparatus is the Head of Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency. 10. Board is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of development planning and regional research. 11. Head of Board is a Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning. 12. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capacity so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 13. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development policies and programs. 14. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of social construction and can change due to social and cultural circumstances of society. 15. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in the development process. 16. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women. 17. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG, is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 18. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point, hereinafter referred to as Focal Point PUG, is a PD apparatus that has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 19. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD, is the elaboration of the vision, mission and program of the Regent whose preparation is guided by the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, which contains regional development strategies, general regional policies, 3 regional programs and macroeconomic framework that includes an overview of the economy as a whole including the direction of fiscal policy in a work plan in the form of a regulatory framework and funding framework that is indicative. 20. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in development and the benefits they enjoy. 21. Gender Responsive Budget is a performance-based budget allocation for certain programs or activities whose input, output, and outcome indicators can ensure the fulfillment of the aspirations and needs of women and men fairly. 22. Communication, Information and Education, hereinafter abbreviated as KIE, is the delivery of messages in the form of information, ideas or facts related to gender mainstreaming that need to be known by the community directly or indirectly through communication channels to message recipients to obtain effects, as a process of behavioral change towards gender responsiveness. 23. District Development Planning Deliberation, hereinafter referred to as Musrembangcam, is a deliberation forum among development actors to discuss and agree on steps to handle priority program activities listed in the list of proposed village development planning activities that are integrated with development priorities of North Central Timor Regency in the district area coordinated by the Regional Development Planning Board and implemented by the District Head. 25. Work Plan, hereinafter referred to as Renja, is a one-year planning document that contains policies, programs, and development activities both planned directly by Regional Apparatus or pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra. 28. Regional Government Work Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RKPD, is a one-year planning document that contains policies, programs, and development activities both planned directly by the Regional Government or pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra. 29. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is an activity planning document prepared by a technical team to be implemented in a certain period/time. 30.

Article 38

1. The Office is responsible for facilitating family quality improvement activities in the Region.
2. Improving family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented through:
a. facilitating the establishment of service provider institutions;
b. in coordination with PD and/or related institutions that have the main tasks and functions to carry out activities:

2. developing job training for women.

Paragraph 3

Implementation

CHAPTER VIII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 45

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, existing women's protection service provider institutions shall continue to carry out their duties until the establishment of the regional technical implementing unit for the protection of women and children in accordance with the provisions of this Regional Regulation.

Paragraph 2

Coordinator

Article 27

1. PD that administers governmental affairs in the social field is responsible for facilitating Women's Empowerment in the socio-cultural field.
2. Women's Empowerment in the socio-cultural field through:
a. increasing knowledge, attitudes and skills to encourage the fulfillment of tiered education in accordance with potential to improve social status;
b. increasing awareness, willingness and ability to overcome health problems through quality promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts especially in the field of reproductive health;
c. increasing awareness and knowledge about independent, healthy and prosperous family planning including access to consultation services and marriage registration; and
d. facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and the development of science, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

Paragraph 1

General

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2020

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

REGENT OF NORTH CENTRAL TIMOR

HAS DECIDED:

To Enact: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

Supervision

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

I. GENERAL

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.

In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened with the establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This is what needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved with empowerment programs.

The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs through data on civil servants based on gender available in the field.

Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women is conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 24

The implementation of Women's Empowerment in community organizations is carried out by PD in accordance with the main tasks and functions carried out in accordance with regional financial capacity.

Paragraph 1

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women And Children

Article 6

1. The Regent has the authority to establish the PUG Working Group.
2. The establishment of the PUG Working Group as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
3. The Regent's Decree as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be valid for 5 (five) years.
4. The management of the PUG Working Group consists of:
a. chairperson by the head of the agency;
b. secretariat by the head of the office;
c. members including:
1. head of PD;
2. technical team consisting of:
a. apparatus who have attended training or education in gender-responsive budget analysis of at most 5 (five) persons.
b. representatives of university elements of at most 5 (five) persons;
c. press representatives of at most 5 (five) persons; and
d. representatives of non-governmental organizations that have an orientation scope in the field of gender of at most 5 (five) persons.

Gender Analysis Pathway, hereinafter abbreviated as GAP, is a gender analysis tool that can be used to assist planners in mainstreaming gender in planning development policies/programs/activities with the aim of identifying gender gaps and gender issues as well as simultaneously preparing development policy/program/activity plans aimed at reducing or eliminating such gender gaps. 31. Technical Team is a Team formed by Pokja PUG with the task of conducting gender-perspective budget analysis and preparing RAD PUG.

Paragraph 3

Implementation

Paragraph 3

Pokja PUG

Article 20

1. Pokja PUG is responsible for preparing PUG Implementation Reports every 6 (six) months and five-yearly RAD PUG Implementation Reports.
2. The reporting framework as referred to in paragraph (1) is guided by the reporting framework as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning General Guidelines for PUG Implementation in the Region.
3. Pokja PUG Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) are reported to the Regent.
4. The Regent is responsible for examining and stating approval of Pokja PUG Reports as referred to in paragraph (1).
5. The Regent is responsible for sending pokja PUG reports as referred to in paragraph (1) to the Minister who administers Home Affairs governmental affairs.

Article 36

1. The Office may provide assistance to Service Institutions located in the region in the form of:
a. strengthening Service Institutions; and
b. development of Service Institutions
2. Strengthening service institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through:
a. improving the competence of service institution members; and/or
b. facilitating paralegal training on a regular basis
3. Development of Service Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through:
a. providing additional facilities and infrastructure;
b. providing information technology-based service approaches; and/or
c. recruiting village cadres as paralegal assistants.
